subject: physics
question_text: What is the time period of revolution of a geostationary satellite? Does it revolve from west to east or from east to west?

verification.note: The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The time period
lines: A geostationary satellite keeps exact pace
with the earth’s own rotation, so its time
period equals one rotation of the earth:
steps.why: Anything other than 24 hours and the satellite would drift over the ground instead of staying put.
common_mistakes: Giving 12 hours, or the ~90 minutes of a low-orbit satellite.

recall.must_convey: That the time period is 24 hours, the same as the rotation of the earth.

steps.memory_tip: 24 hours — exactly the earth’s own spin period.

steps.label: The direction
lines: That is the direction in which the earth
itself rotates. Only by matching BOTH the
period and the direction can the satellite
stay above the same point on the ground.
steps.why: Matching the period alone is not enough — a satellite going the other way would pass overhead twice a day.
common_mistakes: Answering east to west, the direction the sun appears to move.

recall.must_convey: That it revolves from west to east, the same direction as the earth rotates.
accept: same direction as the earth rotates

steps.memory_tip: West to east — the same direction the earth turns.
